transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?

Well, I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just... paperwork and missed payments. But I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. They can say whatever they want, but no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years now.

You mentioned you've been seeing evidence of this coordination for almost two years. If the bank showed you documents proving the loan was processed normally without any coordination with your employer, would that change your mind about what's been happening?

No, it wouldn't. Like I just said, no amount of paperwork they show me is going to change my mind. 

It's easy enough to make documents look like a standard process when you're trying to cover something up. I manage a retail floor, I know how paper trails work. They can print out whatever forms they want, but a stack of normal-looking loan papers doesn't erase what I've actually been seeing with my own eyes for the last two years. I know they are working together, and a piece of paper saying otherwise doesn't make that go away.
Besides what's happening with the bank and your job, have you noticed other people or groups working against you or trying to harm you in other areas of your life?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. It's really just... just the people at the bank and my job. I don't think there's anyone else trying to harm me or work against me in other parts of my life. It's strictly this specific situation with my house and the people involved in that.

When you think about this situation with the bank and your job, is there any possibility—even a small one—that you might be misinterpreting what's happening, or do you feel completely certain that they are coordinating against you?

I am completely certain. There's really no... no possibility that I'm misinterpreting it. 

I know everyone keeps acting like this is just a normal foreclosure, just paperwork and missed payments, but I know what I've been seeing for almost two years now. The bank, the loan servicer, the people at my job—they are quietly working together to push me out of my house. I'm not confused about it, and I'm not making a mistake. I know exactly what they're doing.

Besides what you've been seeing with your own eyes about the bank and your job coordinating against you, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people around you couldn't hear, or experienced other unusual perceptions?

No, I haven't heard any voices or anything like that. I don't see things that aren't there or hear sounds other people don't hear. It's just the actual things happening with the bank and my job. Nothing else.
When you think about why the bank and your job are working together to push you out of your house, do you have a clear understanding of their specific reasons or motives for doing this to you?

I don't... I don't really know why they chose me, to be honest. That's the part I haven't figured out. I just know that they are doing it. I don't know what their exact motive is or what they get out of targeting my specific house, but the actions are there. The proof is in what they're doing, even if I don't understand the "why" behind it yet.

You mentioned the bank, the loan servicer, and people at your job are working together. Can you walk me through how you think they're communicating or coordinating with each other? What specific actions or signs have shown you they're in contact?

I don't really know exactly how they're communicating. I don't have, like, emails or recordings of their phone calls to show you. I just know that they are. The timing is just... it's too perfect. Whenever the bank sends a notice, my boss suddenly cuts my hours or changes my schedule so I can't pick up extra shifts. It's like they know exactly when to squeeze me. I haven't seen them talking, but they have to be. It's the only thing that makes sense with how it's all happening at the exact same time.

Over these past two years while you've been noticing this coordination between the bank and your job, have you noticed any changes in how well you're able to do your work, maintain friendships, or take care of daily responsibilities like paying bills or keeping your home clean?

Well, honestly, my day-to-day life is mostly fine. I mean, I still get up every day and go to work. I supervise my team, I make sure the schedules are sorted, I deal with customer complaints... all of that is normal. I still take care of myself and keep the house clean. 

The only time things get difficult is when it has to do with the foreclosure stuff. Like, if I get a piece of mail from the bank, or a phone call, or if there's some paperwork at my job that feels like it's connected to them trying to push me out. That's when I get distracted or stressed out. But as long as it doesn't involve the house situation, I'm functioning just fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a circumscribed delusional system involving a coordinated conspiracy by the bank, loan servicer, and employer to force foreclosure. Key diagnostic features supporting F22.0 (Delusional Disorder, Paranoid Type): (1) Non-bizarre delusion held with absolute conviction for nearly 2 years; (2) Resistance to contradictory evidence (explicitly stated that documents would not change his mind); (3) Complete certainty with no insight into possible misinterpretation; (4) Absence of hallucinations or other psychotic symptoms; (5) Functional impairment limited to areas directly related to the delusional content; (6) Preserved functioning in work, self-care, and social domains unrelated to the delusion. The delusion is internally consistent but lacks verifiable evidence (timing coincidences interpreted as coordination without documented communication). This presentation is classic for delusional disorder rather than brief psychotic disorder (duration >1 month, stable), schizophrenia (no hallucinations or disorganization), or adjustment disorder (primary feature is fixed delusion, not stress response).
